Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The round has thirteen stations, from the gate to the fan deck.
  • The pictures show the equipment as the operator meets it.
  • Three working levels: pit, grade and fan deck; the pit is all local.
2

Part 2

What can only be read in the field, and how is a reading judged?

Part 2 · the plan

Readings

  1. Local-only gaugeslevel board, pump gauges, filter ΔP, cold-water thermometers
  2. The rounds sheet28 items, each checked against the plant within a tolerance
  3. Into the event logevery reading is logged for the exercises

Part 2 · step through

Twenty-eight items on every round

The rounds sheet is the log the outside operator fills in on every round.

Check compares each entry with the plant at that moment, within its tolerance.

Part 2 · try it

Within tolerance or not?

Tolerances follow the instrument: 0.5 °C on temperatures, 10 kPa on pressures, 0.15 on pH.

Part 2 · the event log

Every reading is evidence

TimeTypeLogged
00:43:30FIELDField: checked P-218 (stopped)
00:43:45FIELDRead FT-201 = 340 m³/h
00:44:00FIELDRead TT-201 = 50.4 °C
00:44:30FIELDRead TT-202 = 34.0 °C

From the TE-1 worked example (Systematic problem solving).

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Some readings exist only in the field: the level board, pump gauges, filter ΔP, cold-water points.
  • Each rounds-sheet item has its own tolerance.
  • Readings go into the event log, where the exercises and the workbook use them.
3

Part 3

What does a hand valve do to the plant?

Part 3 · the plan

Hand valves

  1. Handwheel and leverrising stem: stem up = open; quarter-turn: along the pipe = open
  2. Real effectsa closed suction or discharge takes its pump out
  3. Car-sealed valveslocked open or closed: a permit is needed

Part 3 · try it

What the discharge gauge says

Hand valves of the EPC P&ID are in the model, with their real effects.

Closing a valve in the field does to the plant what it would do for real, and the gauge shows it.

Part 3 · try it

Some valves must not move without a permit

The seal is a barrier against the well-meant mistake; the permit makes the move deliberate.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Rising stems and lever handles show the position at a glance.
  • A closed suction runs a pump dry; a closed discharge deadheads it at about 500 kPa g.
  • Car-sealed valves need a permit; every move is logged.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the round in order and log every station.

2

Read the field-only gauges: the DCS cannot see them.

3

Judge each reading against its tolerance, and re-read when it fails.

4

Treat a hand valve as a real handle: check what it isolates before moving it.

Open the tab in the simulator and try each point on the live plant.
